NDIS / Home Care Information

Making sense of disability support & home care

A plain-language guide to how support is funded and organised in Australia — so you can make decisions with confidence.

General information only. Everything on this page is general information about the NDIS and home care in Australia. It is not a description of Niyah Care Services’ own offering — the supports we will provide are to be confirmed, and nothing here should be read as a claim about our registration status or services. For advice about your own situation, please speak with the NDIA, your support coordinator, or an aged care assessor.

The NDIS

What is the NDIS?

The National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) is Australia’s national scheme for people living with a significant and permanent disability. Instead of funding going to organisations, funding is provided to the participant, who can choose the providers and supports that suit their goals.

In general terms, a person may be eligible if they are under 65 when they first apply, are an Australian citizen, permanent resident or hold a Protected Special Category visa, and live with a disability that substantially affects their everyday life. Eligibility is assessed by the National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA).

Once approved, a participant receives an NDIS plan with funding across budget categories, which can be managed in different ways — self-managed, plan-managed, or NDIA-managed.

Illustrative photography.

NDIS Funding

The three NDIS support budgets

NDIS plans generally organise funding into three categories. These are general descriptions of the scheme — not services offered by any particular provider.

Core Supports

Everyday assistance that helps a participant complete daily activities — such as help around the home, personal care, community access and transport.

Capacity Building

Supports that build skills and independence over time — for example life skills, community participation, employment-related support and improved daily living.

Capital Supports

Higher-cost items such as assistive technology and home or vehicle modifications, which are quoted and approved individually within a plan.

Illustrative photography.

Home Care

Support at home for older Australians

For older Australians, government-subsidised home care helps people live independently at home for as long as possible. Access generally begins with an assessment arranged through My Aged Care, the Australian Government’s entry point for aged care services.

Depending on assessed needs, home care can include help with personal care, domestic tasks, meals, transport, social support and respite for carers. The level of funding and the services available depend on the individual assessment and program rules at the time.

Whether support comes through the NDIS or through aged care, the principle is the same: the person receiving support should have choice and control over how it is delivered.

Common Questions

Frequently asked questions

In general terms, the NDIS supports people under 65 living with a significant and permanent disability. Government-funded home care supports older Australians, generally 65 and over (or 50 and over for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people), assessed through My Aged Care. The two systems have different eligibility rules and funding arrangements.
Yes — choice and control sit at the heart of the NDIS. How much choice you have can depend on how your plan is managed: self-managed and plan-managed participants generally have the widest choice of providers, while NDIA-managed plans typically use registered providers.
Our final service offering is currently being confirmed. The sample support areas on our Services page show the kinds of help we are working towards, clearly marked as “to be confirmed”. Please send us an enquiry to discuss your needs and be among the first to know when services are confirmed.
Applications are made directly with the government schemes: the NDIA handles NDIS access requests, and My Aged Care arranges aged care assessments. Their contact details are published on their official government channels — we have not listed phone numbers here because ours are still to be confirmed, and we would never want to give you a wrong number.

Working With Us

Working with Niyah Care Services

Our team is the heart of everything we do. Working with Niyah Care Services means being part of a person-centred team where relationships come first — with the people we support, their families, and each other.

The work is varied and deeply rewarding: one day you might be supporting someone to build independence skills at home, the next you are out in the community helping them pursue a goal they have been working towards. What never changes is the difference you make.

We welcome expressions of interest from people who are compassionate, reliable and respectful — whether you are experienced in disability or aged care support, or looking to begin a meaningful new career.
